attempts.label: DANDI:001605
attempts.paper_title: Neural substrate of dynamic Bayesian inference in the cerebral cortex
attempts.entry_title: Dynamic Bayesian inference in mouse PPC and PM (Funamizu, Kuhn and Doya 2016)
attempts.summary: Most of this paper's behavioural and decoding findings that could be tested held up in this data, but the neuron-class counts did not reproduce, and several central tests could not be run. The licking increase without sound, PPC's larger share of goal-distance neurons, ramping activity in PPC after-reaching neurons, and lower decoder uncertainty with sound in PPC reproduced. The neuron-class counts (12 to 41% above the paper's for most groups), time to reward (9.3 s against 7.4 s) and the log-normal decoder's advantage did not reproduce. The muscimol experiments could not be tested because the dandiset lacks those mice. Findings that depend on the unstated baseline of the task-relevance test, or on the chance level of the decoder, were blocked because the readings disagree.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Funamizu, Kuhn and Doya (2016) on dandiset 001605, which holds the two-photon imaging and behaviour of 94 sessions in 8 mice during auditory virtual navigation. It checks the session and neuron counts, licking behaviour, the classification of task-relevant neurons, the ramping of after-reaching neurons with and without sound, and the probabilistic decoding of goal distance. The muscimol experiment and the sound-mapping trials are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Funamizu et al. (2016) from dandiset 001605

outcomes.statement: Imaging data come from 94 sessions of 8 mice (2, 10, 5, 14, 15, 15, 12 and 21 sessions for mice 1 to 8); PPC layers 2, 3 and 5 were imaged in 17, 15 and 14 sessions and PM layers 2, 3 and 5 in 16, 15 and 17.
outcomes.source: Online Methods, Behavioral analysis; Results, Goal-distance representation in PPC and PM, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: In total, we analyzed data from 94 sessions in 8 mice (mouse 1, 2 sessions; mouse 2, 10 sessions; mouse 3, 5 sessions; mouse 4, 14 sessions; mouse 5, 15 sessions; mouse 6, 15 sessions; mouse 7, 12 sessions; mouse 8, 21 sessions)
outcomes.notes: 94 files of 8 mice, sessions per mouse 2, 10, 5, 14, 15, 15, 12 and 21 for the labels mouse1 to mouse8 (the paper's list in its order), and 17, 15, 14 PPC and 16, 15, 17 PM sessions in layers 2, 3 and 5. Every count matches.

outcomes.statement: 41,031 neurons were imaged, 8,371, 7,108 and 4,859 in PPC layers 2, 3 and 5 and 7,788, 7,005 and 5,900 in PM; these are active cells, 99.6% of the manually selected ROIs.
outcomes.source: Results, Goal-distance representation in PPC and PM, paragraph 1; Supplementary Table 1
outcomes.quote: In total, we imaged the activity of 41,031 neurons in 94 sessions (PPC ... 8,371, 7,108 and 4,859 neurons from 17, 15 and 14 sessions in layers 2, 3 and 5, respectively; PM ... 7,788, 7,005 and 5,900 neurons from 16, 15 and 17 sessions, respectively)
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a), all ROIs in the files, the counts equal the paper's active-neuron counts exactly, so the files hold the active ROIs only. Reading (b) was not run, since the criterion needs one reading.

outcomes.statement: Mice got the reward 7.4 ± 0.1 s after the trial start and spent 860 ± 10 ms in each no-sound zone of the intermittent conditions (mean ± s.e.m. over 94 sessions).
outcomes.source: Online Methods, Behavioral training, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: Mice got the reward in 7.4 ± 0.1 s (mean ± s.e.m., n = 94). In intermittent conditions, mice spent 860 ± 10 ms (n = 94) in each no-sound zone.
outcomes.notes: Start tone (first frame of the trial record) to the first reward edge, 9.30 s, s.e.m. 0.11 s over 94 sessions (session means 7.39 to 12.66 s), against 7.4 +- 0.1 s. To reaching the goal 9.18 s; from the end of the 970 ms start tone 8.33 s. Time per no-sound zone 1.009 +- 0.020 s under reading (a) and 0.896 +- 0.016 s under reading (b), against 0.86 +- 0.01 s. Both parts fail under every reading. Over all analysed trials the median is 8.83 s and 22.1% of trials are under 7.4 s; every frame series in every file stores a rate of 30.9 Hz, the rate used, and trial start times step by the trial's frames at that rate. Trials over 20 s to reward are 0.48% per session, against 2.71% in the paper; with longer times to reward the data still have fewer slow trials, so the difference does not come from the exclusion.
deviations: The trial start is taken as the first frame of each trial record, where sound_on_off marks the start tone; the paper does not say from which event its 7.4 s is measured.

outcomes.statement: In every session the start-to-first-lick distance correlated with the start-to-goal distance, with r from 0.258 to 0.822 over the 94 sessions (r = 0.798 in the example session).
outcomes.source: Results, Licking indicates action-dependent distance estimation, paragraph 2; Figure 1b; Online Methods, Behavioral analysis
outcomes.quote: Mice increased licking frequency as they approached the goal (r = 0.798, P = 2.11 × 10−34; Fig. 1b; 94 sessions of 8 mice ... r = 0.258 to 0.822, P = 0.00229 to 9.05 × 10−38)

statistics.about: largest P of the 94 sessions (range 0.00229 to 9.05e-38)

outcomes.notes: Pearson r (reading a) is positive with P < 0.01 in all 94 sessions (largest P 0.0079) and spans 0.218 to 0.822; the upper value matches the paper's 0.822, but two sessions (0.218 and 0.227) fall below the criterion's lower bound of 0.232. Spearman (reading b) gives 5 sessions with P >= 0.01 and r from 0.151. The criterion is not met under either reading. The onset variants do worse, the first non-zero frame ('any') r from 0.003 and the first rise from 0 Hz ('bout') 6 sessions with P >= 0.01. The lick frequency is non-zero at the frame passing 33 cm in a median 22% of trials per session (2 to 90%), and a value below the cap is held for a median of 4 frames, so only a change of the value marks a new lick; the 'change' onset is the reading the data support.
deviations: The files hold a lick frequency (1/inter-lick interval, capped at 10 Hz, held between licks), not lick times. The first lick is the first frame beyond 33 cm from the start where this frequency changes to a non-zero value or stays at the cap. Two variants are shown, the first frame of non-zero frequency beyond 33 cm and the first rise from 0 Hz beyond 33 cm.

outcomes.statement: Licking increased as mice approached the goal in all conditions, and in both intermittent conditions it increased even within the no-sound zones (41.9-25.1 and 8.4-0 cm in intermittent 1, 25.1-8.4 cm in intermittent 2).
outcomes.source: Figure 1c; Results, Licking indicates action-dependent distance estimation, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: In intermittent conditions, anticipatory licking increased even when the sound was omitted (one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, P = 4.87 × 10−8 to 1.22 × 10−15; Fig. 1c)

statistics.about: intermittent 1, the four marked bins (largest P)
continuous, the four marked bins (largest P)
intermittent 2, the four marked bins (largest P)
the four no-sound comparisons of both intermittent conditions (range 4.87e-8 to 1.22e-15)

outcomes.notes: One-sided signed-rank tests over 94 sessions; the four no-sound comparisons rise with z = 7.37 and 5.79 (intermittent 1, 29.4-25.2 and 4.2-0 cm) and 6.32 and 5.41 (intermittent 2, 21.0-16.8 and 12.6-8.4 cm), all P < 1e-7; the four continuous comparisons z = 7.42 to 8.42. All other comparisons also rise with P < 0.01 (intermittent 2 at 29.4-25.2 cm, P = 0.0007). Five of eight mice rise in all four no-sound comparisons by their session medians.
deviations: Lick counts per bin are the integral of the lick frequency over the frames in the bin (the files hold no lick times). Bin edges are multiples of 4.2 cm from the goal, as the criterion says; the bins are labelled 29.4-25.2 cm where the claims file writes 29.3-25.1.

outcomes.statement: During no-sound zones licking rose more steeply in fast-locomotion trials than in slow ones, in both intermittent conditions.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 1; Results, Licking indicates action-dependent distance estimation, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Slope of licking ... was significantly steeper in fast trials than slow trials, suggesting that mice use action-dependent distance estimation
outcomes.notes: The readings of O9 disagree, and the criterion needs every reading. In the no-sound zone nearest the goal (zone reading b), fast trials have steeper lick slopes than slow trials in both conditions under both speed readings (speed over the trial, z = 3.06, P = 0.0022 and z = 2.72, P = 0.0066; speed in the zone, z = 3.21, P = 0.0013 and z = 2.92, P = 0.0035). Averaged over every no-sound zone (zone reading a) the difference is not significant (P 0.013 to 0.79). The panel titles of Supplementary Fig. 1 name the zone of reading (b); whether O9 should be narrowed to it is asked of a reader (questions/001605.yaml). The claim would be reproduced under reading (b) alone.
deviations: Lick frequency is the files' lick_rate series. Both readings of O9 for speed and for zones are run.

outcomes.statement: Silencing PPC with muscimol lowered the correlation between start-to-lick and start-to-goal distance, making lick initiation more variable.
outcomes.source: Figure 1d; Results, Licking indicates action-dependent distance estimation, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Correlation coefficients decreased after muscimol injection, indicating that silencing of PPC made lick initiation more variable (Mann-Whitney U test, P = 3.08 × 10−4, z = 3.61)

statistics.n: muscimol against PBS sessions of 3 mice (12 of each, read from Fig. 1f)

outcomes.notes: The muscimol and PBS sessions of three further mice are not in the dandiset, which holds 94 imaging sessions of the 8 imaging mice only (all files have imaging data and an imaging-plane description). While preparing the entry, outside the notebook, the paper's data page https://groups.oist.jp/ncu/data was fetched and its text named no file for this paper; this check is not shown in the notebook and supplies no number. No other deposit was found.

outcomes.statement: After muscimol the distance between the first lick and the goal was more variable than after PBS, in all three conditions.
outcomes.source: Figure 1e; Results, Licking indicates action-dependent distance estimation, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Variance of the distance was compared between PBS and muscimol-injected trials
outcomes.notes: Muscimol sessions not in the dandiset nor found elsewhere (see fig1d-muscimol-correlation).

outcomes.statement: After muscimol, licking no longer increased significantly in the no-sound zones of the intermittent conditions, while after PBS it did. The increase of licks between adjacent bins in those no-sound zones was smaller after muscimol than after PBS.
outcomes.source: Figure 1f,g; Results, Licking indicates action-dependent distance estimation, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: The effect of PPC silencing was most prominent in intermittent conditions, with no increase in licking in no-sound zones (one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, P = 0.485 to 0.0212; Fig. 1f; Mann-Whitney U-test, P = 0.00761 and 4.84 × 10−6; Fig. 1g)

statistics.about: muscimol, no-sound bins of intermittent conditions (range 0.485 to 0.0212)
PBS against muscimol, increase from 25-17 to 17-8.4 cm, intermittent 2
PBS against muscimol, increase from 17-8.4 to 8.4-0 cm, intermittent 1

outcomes.notes: Muscimol sessions not in the dandiset nor found elsewhere (see fig1d-muscimol-correlation).

outcomes.statement: Silencing PPC increased overrun, the start of licking more than 8.3 cm past the goal, most in the intermittent 1 condition.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 2d; Results, Licking indicates action-dependent distance estimation, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Silencing of PPC increased overrun (start licking over 8.3 cm past the goal)
outcomes.notes: Muscimol sessions not in the dandiset nor found elsewhere (see fig1d-muscimol-correlation).

outcomes.statement: PPC inactivation lowered locomotion speed and raised anticipatory licking in the continuous condition, but changed neither in the intermittent conditions.
outcomes.source: Online Methods, Muscimol injection, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Inactivation of PPC decreased the locomotion speed of mice in the continuous condition (MannWhitney U-test, P = 9.63 × 10−12, z = 6.81), which was most probably caused by increased anticipatory licking (Mann-Whitney U-test, P = 6.92 × 10−11, z = 6.52). In intermittent conditions, inactivation of PPC did not change the locomotion speed (P = 0.106, z = 1.62) and the licking (P = 0.0828, z = 1.73).
outcomes.notes: Muscimol sessions not in the dandiset nor found elsewhere (see fig1d-muscimol-correlation).

outcomes.statement: PPC and PM neurons responded to sounds; in layer 3, PM had more sound-responsive neurons than PPC (4.78% against 1.48%).
outcomes.source: Results, Goal-distance representation in PPC and PM, paragraph 2; Supplementary Figure 4b
outcomes.quote: On average, PM had more sound-responsive neurons than PPC in layer 3 (PPC, 1.48%, PM, 4.78%; Mann-Whitney U test, P = 0.0402)
outcomes.notes: The sound-mapping trials recorded before each imaging session (120 presentations of 200 ms) are not in the files. Every file starts at its first task trial, and the trial frames sum to the series length in all 94 files; sound_on_off and any speaker of stimulus/presentation/speaker_on_matrix (12 speakers) are on in exactly 150 frames, the first frame of each trial (both printed in the data check for all 94 files). In all 94 files every row of speaker_presentations starts at a trial start (largest distance 0 s) and lasts one frame (0.03236 s); there are 150 distinct start times per file and 6 to 26 rows per trial start, one per speaker listed, which gives the 1,085 to 1,240 rows. Not found elsewhere (see fig1d-muscimol-correlation).

outcomes.statement: Goal-distance neurons numbered 1,116, 1,054 and 483 in PPC layers 2, 3 and 5 and 601, 479 and 129 in PM; of these, 744, 854 and 367 in PPC and 193, 204 and 54 in PM were after-reaching neurons; per session, on average 65.6, 70.3 and 34.5 in PPC and 37.6, 31.9 and 7.59 in PM were goal-distance neurons.
outcomes.source: Figure 2d; Figure 3c legend; Supplementary Figure 6 legend; Results, Distance prediction with dynamic Bayesian inference, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Number of after-reaching neurons in layers 2, 3, 5 was 744, 854, 367 in PPC and 193, 204, 54 in PM ... (average number of goal-distance neurons in layers 2, 3 and 5; PPC, 65.6, 70.3 and 34.5; PM, 37.6, 31.9 and 7.59)
outcomes.notes: Under O1 a (baseline zero) and either O3 reading, 2 of 12 counts are within 10% (PM layer 2 and 3 goal-distance neurons, 659 and 512); the others are 12 to 41% above the paper's. Under O1 b none is within 10% (goal-distance 1,650, 1,402, 775, 961, 738, 304). O3 changes no count by more than 4. With k-means per session (variant), 5 of 12 counts are within 10% under O1 a and 3 under O1 b. Values recorded are O1 a, O3 a. The order of the groups is the paper's (PPC above PM, layer 5 lowest). Per session the goal-distance neurons average 79.6, 86.1, 39.6, 41.2, 34.1 and 9.3 (paper 65.6, 70.3, 34.5, 37.6, 31.9, 7.59). By mouse the share of goal-distance neurons ranges from 1.4% (mouse2) to 25.6% (mouse3).
deviations: k-means (two clusters) is run once on the after-reaching group pooled over all sessions, with seed 0 and 20 starts; the paper does not say whether it clustered per session. A per-session variant is shown, for the counts and the supp8 claims.
The inter-trial interval of baseline O1 b is the last 7 s of each trial record, from the Methods' "The inter-trial interval (ITI) was 7 s"; the records run 7.9 to 8.2 s past the reward.

Distance-aligned activity is interpolated at 0.42 cm bin centres between the frames from the start to the goal (a standard choice; most 0.42 cm bins hold no frame at the mice's speeds). Moving averages are 15 frames (500 ms) and 20 bins (8.4 cm).

outcomes.statement: Task-relevant neurons made up 41.3, 33.8 and 20.0% of active neurons in PPC layers 2, 3 and 5 and 19.6, 16.7 and 5.70% in PM, more in PPC than in PM in every layer.
outcomes.source: Results, Goal-distance representation in PPC and PM, paragraph 4; Figure 2d
outcomes.quote: Among active neurons (99.6% of all neurons; Supplementary Table 1), the proportions of task-relevant neurons in layers 2, 3 and 5 were 41.3, 33.8 and 20.0% in PPC, and 19.6, 16.7 and 5.70% in PM, indicating that more neurons were recruited to the task in PPC than PM
outcomes.notes: No percentage is within tolerance under any reading of O1, O2 or O5. Recorded is O1 a, O2 0-67 cm, O5 a (mean of per-session percentages); pooled (O5 b) 48.1, 38.1, 25.4, 27.6, 23.5 and 8.1%; under O1 b 52.7 to 12.7%. PPC exceeds PM in every layer; Mann-Whitney P < 0.05 in layers 2 and 5 under every reading (P <= 0.0011), and in layer 3 P = 0.051 under O1 a and 0.023 to 0.025 under O1 b, so the second part holds under O1 b only.

outcomes.statement: PPC had more goal-distance neurons than PM in all three layers.
outcomes.source: Results, Goal-distance representation in PPC and PM, paragraph 4; Figure 2d
outcomes.quote: PPC had more goal-distance neurons than PM in all layers (Mann-Whitney U test, P = 0.00415, 0.0152 and 4.98 × 10−4, z = 2.87, 2.43 and 3.48, respectively; Fig. 2d)
outcomes.notes: PPC exceeds PM in all three layers, as proportions and as counts, under all four O1 and O3 readings (Mann-Whitney P 0.0002 to 0.013). Under O1 a, proportions P = 0.0030, 0.0090 and 0.0005.

outcomes.statement: PPC had more after-reaching than before-reaching neurons in every layer, whereas PM tended the other way, significantly in layer 2.
outcomes.source: Results, Goal-distance representation in PPC and PM, paragraph 4; Figure 2d
outcomes.quote: PPC had more after-reaching neurons than before-reaching neurons (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, P = 0.0319, 0.00568 and 0.0176, z = 2.15, w = 13.5 and 9.5), whereas PM had the opposite tendency (P = 0.00771, 0.287 and 0.427, z = 2.66, w = 70 and 57.5)
outcomes.notes: The readings of O1 disagree. Under O1 a (zero baseline), PPC has more after- than before-reaching neurons in layers 2, 3 and 5 (counts P = 0.0086, 0.0038, 0.011; proportions 0.0086, 0.0038, 0.0060), PM layer 2 has more before-reaching neurons (P = 0.0038 counts, 0.0045 proportions) and PM layers 3 and 5 do not differ (P 0.39 to 0.64), so the criterion holds. Under O1 b (inter-trial baseline), PPC does not differ in any layer (P 0.07 to 0.52) and PM has more before-reaching neurons in all three layers (P <= 0.0013), so it fails. The claims file's header blocks a claim whose readings disagree.

outcomes.statement: In both PPC and PM, goal-distance neurons in layers 3 and 5 preferred distances closer to the goal than those in layer 2.
outcomes.source: Figure 2d insets and legend; Results, Goal-distance representation in PPC and PM, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: in both areas, goal-distance neurons in layers 3 and 5 were more tuned to the distance near the goal than those in layer 2 (Mann-Whitney U test, P = 0.00319 to 2.25 × 10−16)
outcomes.notes: The readings of O1 disagree. Under O1 a, layer 3 and layer 5 goal-distance neurons prefer distances nearer the goal than layer 2 in PPC (z = 7.93 and 4.59, P < 1e-5) and PM (z = 4.19, P = 2e-5; z = 2.61, P = 0.0083). Under O1 b PM layer 5 does not differ from layer 2 (z = -0.88, P = 0.38; medians 14.91 and 22.68 cm), so the criterion fails there.
deviations: Distance preference is the goal distance of the peak of the smoothed distance-aligned average over 67.2 to 0 cm (O4).

outcomes.statement: In PPC and PM, more goal-distance neurons were best fit by goal distance than by the time to reach the goal.
outcomes.source: Figure 3b; Results, Goal-distance representation in PPC and PM, paragraph 6
outcomes.quote: More neurons represented the goal distance than the time to goal in PPC and PM (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, P = 0.00348 to 4.33 × 10−4)
outcomes.notes: The regression fits up to three Gaussian bases with free widths, for 11 variable sets and four initial values, to every frame of 150 trials. In the notebook one three-basis nonlinear least-squares fit on the 19,586 decoder frames of a median session took 0.54 s, so 44 fits for each of the 4,529 goal-distance neurons (O1 a) need about 29.7 h per reading and 118.9 h over the four readings of O6 on one thread, and 29.7 h over the notebook's 4 workers, beyond the notebook limit of 60 min. Not run; the data are in the files.

outcomes.statement: Goal-distance and after-reaching neurons were fit better by goal distance than by a distance held constant during no-sound zones or by the sound intensity.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 6; Results, Goal-distance representation in PPC and PM, paragraph 6
outcomes.quote: RMSE of Distance was significantly smaller than of other variables both in goal-distance neurons and after-reaching neurons, indicating goal distance representation
outcomes.notes: Distance has the lower RMSE with P < 0.05 in 23 of 24 comparisons under every reading (frames O6 a and b, sound readings a and b, all four classification readings). The exception is PM layer 5 after-reaching neurons against Step (P = 0.11, n = 76 under O1 a). The criterion's partial threshold is 20. Differences of median RMSE are below 0.002 dR/R.
deviations: The free width is profiled over a grid of 25 log-spaced values from 0.5 to 200 (cm or dB), with the linear coefficients fitted by least squares at each, and refined by a bounded scalar optimizer of the log width between the neighbouring grid values, in place of an optimizer from four initial values (Online Methods, Regression analysis). The basis centre is the value of the variable at the peak of the neuron's activity averaged in 0.42 cm (1 dB for Sound) bins and smoothed over 20 bins (3 for Sound).

Sound intensity follows the Methods (100 dB SPL at 25 cm, 6 dB lower per doubling); Step holds the goal distance on entering each no-sound zone. Zones are computed from the condition and distance, as the files hold no task sound.

outcomes.statement: The distance tuning curves of goal-distance neurons, as fitted coefficients, did not differ between PPC and PM.
outcomes.source: Results, Goal-distance representation in PPC and PM, paragraph 6
outcomes.quote: Fitted coefficients for goal-distance representation revealed that the distance tuning curves of neurons were similar between PPC and PM (Online Methods; Mann-Whitney U test, P = 0.268 to 0.106, z = 1.11 to 1.62)

statistics.about: PPC against PM, per layer (smallest P of the range)

outcomes.notes: The readings disagree, and the criterion directs a block. Widths are fitted continuously (grid then bounded optimizer). With frames O6 a, PPC and PM differ in the width s in all three layers (P 3e-12 to 0.024) and in b1 in layers 3 and 5 under every classification reading (P 2e-11 to 0.016), and in layer 2 under O1 b (P = 0.014). With frames O6 b and O1 a the widths do not differ (P 0.083 to 0.21), while b1 differs in all three layers (P 4e-10 to 0.0085); under O1 b with frames O6 b the width differs in layer 5 (P = 0.0052). Open for the authors which coefficient the comparison used and over which frames the fits ran (finding below).
deviations: The fit is the distance-only set of equation (2), y = b0 + b1 phi(distance), with the width profiled over a grid as in supp6-distance-not-sound.

outcomes.statement: In the continuous condition, after-reaching neurons increased their activity as mice approached the goal, in both PPC and PM.
outcomes.source: Figure 3c; Results, PPC represents goal distance estimated from action, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Activity in the continuous condition gradually increased in both PPC and PM as mice approached the goal (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, P = 0.00507 to 0, z = 2.80 to 25.0; Fig. 3c, and Supplementary Figs. 7 and 8a)

statistics.about: all area, layer and zone tests (largest P)

outcomes.notes: All 12 area, layer and zone tests positive with P < 0.01 under all four classification readings and both trace readings (z 6.3 to 27.9 under O1 a, trace a; n 76 to 1,061 neurons).

outcomes.statement: In the intermittent conditions, PPC after-reaching neurons in all layers increased activity toward the goal both with and without sound.
outcomes.source: Figure 3c; Supplementary Figure 8a; Results, PPC represents goal distance estimated from action, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: In intermittent conditions, increased activity was observed with and without sound inputs in all PPC layers (sound zones ... P = 1.37 × 10−4 to 0, z = 3.81 to 23.2; no-sound zones ... P = 1.19 × 10−6 to 0, z = 4.86 to 17.9)
outcomes.notes: All 12 PPC tests positive with P < 0.01 under every reading, including the six no-sound tests (z 5.6 to 15.4 under O1 a, trace a).

outcomes.statement: In PM, after-reaching neurons showed positive slopes in some no-sound zones, but in the intermittent 1 condition their slopes without sound were not significantly positive.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 8a; Results, PPC represents goal distance estimated from action, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Slopes were significantly positive with and without sound in PPC in all conditions, but in PM in intermittent 1 condition they were not significantly positive without sound.

statistics.about: PM, no-sound zones with positive slopes (Results; range 2.40e-4 to 0)

outcomes.notes: The readings disagree. Under O1 a and trace reading (a), PM intermittent 2 no-sound slopes at 25.1-8.4 cm are positive with P < 0.01 in all three layers (z 5.3 to 7.6), and intermittent 1 at 8.4-0 cm in none (P = 0.47, 0.57, 0.017), so the criterion holds. With the moving average (trace b) or O1 b, layer 5 in intermittent 1 has P < 0.01 (P = 0.0026 under O1 a with trace b), so the absence part fails. With k-means per session (variant) one intermittent 1 test has P < 0.01 under every reading.
deviations: Both trace readings of the claims file are run, the 0.42 cm bins and the 8.37 cm moving average.

outcomes.statement: Slopes of after-reaching activity were lower without sound than with sound.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 8b
outcomes.quote: Although slopes were significantly positive even without sound in a, they were less steep than those with sound
outcomes.notes: The readings of O1 disagree. Slopes without sound are lower with P < 0.01 in all six PPC comparisons under every reading. PM has four of six under O1 a (PM layer 5, P = 0.029 and 0.017), as the criterion needs, and three of six under O1 b. With k-means per session (variant), PM has four under O1 a and two under O1 b.

outcomes.statement: Without sound, PPC after-reaching neurons in layers 2 and 3 had steeper slopes than PM, while slopes in PM were equal to or lower than in PPC.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 8c; Results, PPC represents goal distance estimated from action, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: In layers 2 and 3, PPC had steeper slopes than PM without sound
outcomes.notes: The readings disagree. Under O1 a and trace (a), PPC no-sound slopes exceed PM in layer 2 (8.4-0 cm, P = 0.0010) and layer 3 (8.4-0 cm, P = 0.0006), and PM is significantly steeper in no comparison, but layer 3 at 25.1-8.4 cm does not differ (P = 0.59; 0.10 with trace b), so the criterion fails. Under O1 b with trace (b) all parts hold (layer 3 at 25.1-8.4 cm P = 0.013). The criterion is met in 2 of the 8 classification and trace readings, and in none of the 8 with k-means per session (variant).

outcomes.statement: PPC neurons kept the distance preference they had in the continuous condition in the intermittent conditions, especially near the goal, more than PM neurons did.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 9b; Results, PPC represents goal distance estimated from action, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: PPC neurons preserved the distance representation, especially near the goal, significantly more than neurons in PM (Mann-Whitney U test, P = 0.0429 to 6.82 × 10−14, z = 2.02 to 7.49)
outcomes.notes: Changed by the reader's answer (questions/001605.yaml). The first run tested absolute differences and was reproduced under the assumptions O1 a and groups (a). The amended criterion tests the signed difference, continuous minus intermittent, judges the area whose median is nearer zero, and needs both group readings. In intermittent 1 after-reaching neurons differ with P < 0.05 in layers 2 and 3 (P = 0.0066 and P < 1e-5) with the PPC median nearer zero (-2.10 against -5.04 cm and -2.52 against -6.30 cm); layer 5 does not differ (P = 0.20). With groups (b) none of 9 significant comparisons has the PM median nearer zero; with groups (a) 2 of 10 do, the layer 3 before-reaching groups of intermittent 1 at 67-50.25 cm (PPC 2.52, PM 0.00 cm, P = 0.013) and 50.25-33.5 cm (-9.24 and -1.89 cm, P = 0.037). The criterion fails under groups (a), and so under every O1 and O3 reading; the after-reaching part holds under all, and in the groups nearest the goal every significant comparison has PPC nearer zero; the criterion has no partial outcome. The absolute-difference variant, not judged, has PPC after-reaching smaller in all three layers and PM significantly smaller in 0 of 30 comparisons (groups a) and 1 of 30 (groups b) under O1 a. No assumption decides the outcome now, since the criterion takes both group readings and the O1 readings agree.
deviations: Distance preference per condition is the peak of the condition's trial-averaged 0.42 cm trace after the 8.4 cm moving average.

outcomes.statement: Decoders built from goal-distance neurons estimated goal distance above chance in both PPC and PM.
outcomes.source: Results, Distance prediction with dynamic Bayesian inference, paragraph 2; Figure 4b
outcomes.quote: Both areas estimated the goal distances reliably above chance level (Wilcoxon signed rank test, P = 0, z = 181 to 439)
outcomes.notes: The readings of chance disagree. Decoder RMSE is below the flat prior's (reading a) in all 18 settings under all eight classification and shift readings (z -87.6 to -365.9, P = 0; median RMSE 15.64 cm in continuous trials of the main reading against 26.97 cm). Against decoders trained on distances permuted across trials (reading b), 17 of 18 settings are lower in six readings and 18 of 18 in two; under O1 a and shift 0.01 the exception is PPC layer 3 in intermittent 1 (z = +13.6). Reading (b) keeps the fall of distance within every trial, so its decoder still decodes distance and does not measure chance; this is asked of a reader (questions/001605.yaml). The claim would be reproduced with chance read as the flat prior.
deviations: Decoder details from the claims file and Methods; the positive shift (O7) is run at 0.01 and 0.1. Frames are those from the start to the goal with goal distance 67.2 to 0 cm. Both chance readings of the claims file are run.

outcomes.statement: The decoding error (RMSE) from layer 2 neurons was lower in PPC than in PM.
outcomes.source: Figure 4c; Results, Distance prediction with dynamic Bayesian inference, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: the estimation in PPC had significantly less deviation from the actual distance than in PM (Mann-Whitney ... U-test in layer 2, P = 0.00765 to 0, z = 2.67 to 17.1)

statistics.n: trials, PPC and PM; continuous 1,785 and 1,721, intermittent 1 398 and 362, intermittent 2 367 and 317

outcomes.notes: The readings disagree. Layer 2, O1 a, shift 0.01, 4.2 cm bins; PPC lower median RMSE in 100%, 88% and 88% of bins (continuous, intermittent 1, intermittent 2), significantly lower in 12, 8 and 8 bins, PM significantly lower in none. The criterion holds in 14 of the 16 configurations of classification, shift and bin width, and fails under O1 b with shift 0.1 and 0.42 cm bins, where one intermittent 2 bin favours PM with P < 0.01. Layers 3 and 5 (trials of sessions without goal-distance neurons left out) have PPC lower in 83% and 94% of 48 bins, PM significantly lower in 3 and 1.

outcomes.statement: PPC and PM gave similar MAP estimates, but near the goal PPC estimates were better than PM.
outcomes.source: Figure 4d; Results, Distance prediction with dynamic Bayesian inference, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: PPC and PM had similar MAP estimates, but the estimations near the goal were better in PPC than in PM (P = 0.00549 to 2.47× 10−11, z = 2.78 to 6.68; Fig. 4d)

statistics.about: significant bins near the goal, range 0.00549 to 2.47e-11

outcomes.notes: The readings of the bin width (O8) disagree. With 4.2 cm bins, in the continuous condition both bins in 8.4-0 cm have PPC MAP closer to the actual distance with P < 0.01 and PM closer in none, under every classification and shift reading; 8 to 11 of 16 bins differ. With 0.42 cm bins PM is closer with P < 0.01 in 3 to 8 of the 20 bins near the goal under every reading, so the criterion fails.
deviations: 'Closer' compares each area's median of per-trial mean MAP with the bin centre.

outcomes.statement: The uncertainty (posterior s.d.) of distance estimates was lower in PPC than in PM at every goal distance and in every condition.
outcomes.source: Figure 4e; Results, Distance prediction with dynamic Bayesian inference, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: uncertainty of distance estimation was significantly less in PPC than PM (P = 1.09 × 10−12 to 0, z = 7.12 to 22.9; Fig. 4e)
outcomes.notes: Layer 2; PPC uncertainty is lower with P < 0.01 in all 48 bins of 4.2 cm and all 480 of 0.42 cm in 14 of the 16 configurations; under O1 b with shift 0.1 and 0.42 cm bins, in 479 of 480 (99.8%). The criterion needs every bin under every reading for reproduced and at least 90% for partial, so the outcome is partial under every reading. Layers 3 and 5 are lower in PPC in all 48 bins of 4.2 cm.

outcomes.statement: Decoding errors decreased with sound and increased without it. Within zones, the change per cm of the RMSE difference (intermittent minus continuous) was lower in sound zones than in no-sound zones, in all PPC layers and in PM layers 2 and 3.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 11b,c; Results, Distance prediction with dynamic Bayesian inference, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Decoding errors decreased with sound and increased without sound (Mann-Whitney U test, P = 0.00295 to 1.56 × 10−6, z = 2.97 to 4.80; Supplementary Fig. 11)
outcomes.notes: The dRMSE slope per cm is lower in sound than no-sound zones with P < 0.01 in all three PPC layers under both readings of n and all eight decoder readings. PM reaches it in two of three layers with four zones and in none or one with two zones.

outcomes.statement: In the continuous condition, decoded MAP distances followed the actual distance in all layers of PPC and PM.
outcomes.source: Figure 5a; Results, Distance prediction with dynamic Bayesian inference, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: In the continuous condition, MAPs followed the actual distances in all layers of PPC and PM (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, P = 9.56 × 10−14 to 0, z = 7.45 to 34.1; Fig. 5a)
outcomes.notes: All 24 area, layer and zone tests positive with P < 0.01 under every reading (PPC z 8.9 to 33.9 in the main reading).

outcomes.statement: In the intermittent conditions, MAPs decreased with and without sound in most zones, and in every zone in PPC layers 3 and 5.
outcomes.source: Figure 5a; Results, Distance prediction with dynamic Bayesian inference, paragraph 3; Discussion, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: In intermittent conditions, MAPs decreased with and without sound inputs in most distance zones, and especially in all zones in PPC layers 3 and 5 (sound zones ... P = 0.00293 to 0, z = 2.98 to 14.7; no-sound zones ... P = 6.59 × 10−4 to 0, z = 3.41 to 8.56)
outcomes.notes: Most zones have positive median MAP slopes with P < 0.01 (39 of 48 under O1 a, 42 under O1 b), but PPC layers 3 and 5 reach it in 13 (O1 a) or 14 (O1 b) of 16, and the criterion needs all 16. Failures include the intermittent 1 no-sound zone 8.4-0 cm, where the median slope is 0. There the MAP is 0 cm, the lower end of the decoded range, in 51.6% of frames, and constant over the zone in 18 to 29% of trials per group, nearly all at 0 cm (76 to 99%), against 2.5 to 3.7% of trials in the other intermittent 1 zones. The zero slopes come from the decoder placing the mouse at the goal before the zone ends, not from the 0.84 cm grid. The decoded range, 67.2 to 0 cm, is the claims file's O8 (Fig. 4b legend, "actual goal distances from 67 to 0 cm"); a decoder whose range extends past the goal was not tried, and the failure may depend on that range (see the last finding).
deviations: Frames within 33 cm of the start, which always have sound, are left out of zones that are silent in their condition.

outcomes.statement: MAP slopes were shallower without sound than with sound.
outcomes.source: Figure 5b; Results, Distance prediction with dynamic Bayesian inference, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Slopes of MAPs without sound were lower than those with sound (Mann-Whitney U test, P = 5.14 × 10−12 to 0; Fig. 5b)
outcomes.notes: No-sound MAP slopes are lower with P < 0.01 in all six PPC comparisons and in five (O1 a) or four (O1 b) of six PM comparisons, under both shifts.

outcomes.statement: In intermittent 1, without sound between 8.4 and 0 cm, MAPs decreased more steeply in PPC layer 3 than layer 2, while the s.d. of the estimates did not differ between these layers.
outcomes.source: Results, Distance prediction with dynamic Bayesian inference, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: In the intermittent 1 condition, the decrease of MAPs in PPC layer 3 was significantly steeper than that in layer 2 without sound between 8.4 and 0 cm (Mann-Whitney U test, P = 0.00685, z = 2.70), whereas the s.d. of distance estimation showed no significant difference (P = 0.247, z = 1.16)
outcomes.notes: Intermittent 1, 8.4-0 cm; PPC layer 3 MAP slopes are not steeper than layer 2 (z = 1.48, P = 0.14 under O1 a, shift 0.01; P 0.07 to 0.56 over all readings; medians 0 in both layers, n = 331 and 397 trials). The s.d. slopes do not differ (P 0.06 to 0.66), the second part. The medians are 0 because the MAP stays at 0 cm through the zone in 29% (layer 2) and 27% (layer 3) of trials (see fig5a-map-decreases-without-sound).

outcomes.statement: During no-sound zones, decoded MAPs fell faster in fast-locomotion trials than in slow ones.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 13; Results, Distance prediction with dynamic Bayesian inference, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Slopes of MAPs were steeper in fast trials than slow trials, suggesting action-dependent distance prediction of mice
outcomes.notes: Fast trials have a significantly steeper fall of MAP over time (P < 0.05) in at most three of the four PPC layer 2 and 3 tests under any of the 32 readings (O9 speed and zone, O1, O3, O7), and in one or two under most; the criterion needs all four under every reading.

outcomes.statement: In all PPC layers, between 25.1 and 0 cm, uncertainty of the estimated distance fell more steeply with sound than without, the updating step of dynamic Bayesian inference.
outcomes.source: Figure 5c,d; Results, Distance prediction with dynamic Bayesian inference, paragraph 3; Discussion, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Uncertainty of estimated distance decreased with sound inputs compared with no sound in all layers of PPC between 25.8 and 0 cm (P = 0.0153 to 6.92 × 10−11; Fig. 5c,d)
outcomes.notes: The fall of uncertainty is larger with sound than without with P < 0.05 in all six PPC comparisons under every reading (P <= 0.0003 under O1 a, shift 0.01). PM in three (O1 a) or two (O1 b) of six.

outcomes.statement: In all PPC layers, the uncertainty of the decoded distance (s.d. of the posterior) decreased during sound presentation between 8.4 and 0 cm.
outcomes.source: Figure 5c and legend
outcomes.quote: Uncertainty decreased during sound presentations in PPC between 8.4 cm and 0 cm.
outcomes.notes: At 8.4-0 cm uncertainty falls with P < 0.01 in all six PPC tests of the continuous and intermittent 2 conditions under every reading (z 5.6 to 10.1 in the main reading); intermittent 1 and PM tests are shown (5 of 12 significant in the main reading).

outcomes.statement: The decoder with a log-normal likelihood estimated goal distance better than one with a Gaussian likelihood in 17 of 18 settings, all but PM layer 5 in the continuous condition.
outcomes.source: Online Methods, Probabilistic decoding of goal distance, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: The decoder with log-normal distribution gave better estimates for goal distance than that with a Gaussian distribution in the 18 settings ... except for layer 5 in PM in continuous condition (P = 0.834, z = 0.209)
outcomes.notes: By RMSE the Gaussian decoder is better with P < 0.01 in 15 to 18 of 18 settings and the log-normal one in none. By absolute MAP error the log-normal decoder is better in 11 or 12 of 18 settings and the Gaussian in 5 or 6. The criterion needs 16 under every reading.
deviations: The Gaussian decoder uses raw activity with per-bin mean and s.d., smoothed and resampled as for the log-normal (claims file).

outcomes.statement: An SVM decoder trained on recorded data did not estimate distance better than one trained on trial-shuffled data, except in one setting, so ignoring correlations between neurons cost the decoder little.
outcomes.source: Online Methods, Probabilistic decoding of goal distance, paragraph 8
outcomes.quote: Recorded-SVM did not estimate distance better than shuffled-SVM (one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, P = 0.957 to 1, z = 1.71 to 12.5), except in 1 setting (layer 3 in PM in intermittent1 condition, P = 0.00572, z = 2.53)
outcomes.notes: Leave-one-trial-out training of recorded and shuffled SVMs. In the notebook, on the session of median goal-distance neuron count (37 neurons, 13,664 continuous frames), one linear multiclass SVM (reading a) took 0.53 s and one linear SVM regression (reading b) 0.01 s, so the 9,596 folds of 91 sessions for two decoders take 2.83 h and 0.06 h on one thread under one classification reading. Over the notebook's 4 workers and the 4 classification readings of O1 and O3 (as for the decoder claims) that is about 173 min, and under O1 a O3 a alone 43 min. The notebook had run 23 min when the estimate was made, leaving 37 min of its limit of 60, so neither the whole claim nor one classification reading of it fits. Not run; the data are in the files.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds only the 94 imaging sessions. The muscimol experiment (three further mice, muscimol and PBS sessions, Fig. 1d-g and Supplementary Fig. 2) and the sound-mapping trials recorded before each imaging session (Supplementary Fig. 4) are not in it, and the paper's data page names no other deposit. Six claims cannot be tested.

The description says the files hold "sound on/off indicators", and sound_on_off is described as "any speaker on". In every file sound_on_off and speaker_on_matrix are on only in the first frame of each trial (150 frames), and every speaker_presentations row lasts one frame at a trial start (6 to 26 rows per trial start, one per speaker listed). The task sound of the continuous and intermittent conditions is not recorded, so sound and no-sound zones must be computed from the condition and distance.

Licking is stored as lick_rate, "Lick frequency (0-10 Hz)", a held 1/inter-lick-interval value capped at 10 Hz, without lick times or a description of how it was derived. Lick counts and first licks can only be approximated from it.

Each trial record runs from one start tone to the next, so it holds the reward and the inter-trial interval; the goal time and the first reward edge are not stored per trial and must be derived from the position and reward series. The mean time from the start tone to the reward is 9.30 s (s.e.m. 0.11 s over sessions), against 7.4 +- 0.1 s in the Methods, and 0.48% of trials take over 20 s, against 2.71%.

The files hold exactly the paper's counts (94 sessions, 8 mice, sessions per area and layer, 41,031 ROIs per area and layer equal to the active-neuron counts) and dF_over_F equals (R - mean R)/mean R of RawFluorescence to 3e-5, as the Methods define dR/R. No recording is deposited twice (94 distinct trial sequences).

For the paper's authors. The baseline of the task-relevance t-test is not given. Zero (the session mean of R) and the mean dR/R of the inter-trial intervals give different neuron classes (PPC layer 2 goal-distance neurons 1,353 against 1,650) and different outcomes for fig2d-after-vs-before, fig2d-layer-distance-preference, supp8a, supp8b and supp8c, which are blocked. Under zero, 91 of 94 sessions have goal-distance neurons, as the paper reports; under the inter-trial baseline, 94. Which baseline was used, and was k-means run per session or pooled?

For the paper's authors. The chance level of Fig. 4b, the bin width of the per-trial values of Fig. 4c-e, and the borders of the before-reaching groups of Supplementary Fig. 9 are not given. The two chance readings and the two bin widths give different outcomes for fig4-above-chance and fig4d-map-near-goal, which are blocked. For Supplementary Fig. 9, equal quarters of 67 to 0 cm give two comparisons where PM is better preserved and the zone borders give none. Which coefficient of the distance fit is compared in "fitted coefficients ... were similar between PPC and PM", and over which frames were the regressions fitted (to the goal or past it)? The readings disagree on that claim, which is blocked.

With the decoder as described, a Gaussian likelihood gives lower RMSE than the log-normal one in 15 to 18 of 18 settings, contrary to the Methods' statement, and PPC layer 3 MAP slopes in intermittent 1 near the goal are not steeper than layer 2. These may come from details of the decoder the Methods leave open (the positive shift, the decoded range).

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: The handover of the first run, the executed notebook with the conclusions and summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper under paper/. Round 1 report transcripts/001605/verifier-1-report.md. Its point B12 (decoder neurons selected with all trials, as the paper does) needed no change.

disagreements.reason: Cell 14: the best reading (Pearson, onset "change") has every P < 0.01 (largest 0.0079), but r runs 0.218-0.822. Two sessions fall below 0.232 (0.218, 0.227). Close miss. The lick onset as a change in the held lick frequency is a stated assumption forced by the data, but untested; the "any" variant collapses (r down to 0.003), which suggests the rate does not drop to 0 between bouts, and this detail could decide it (B11).

Cell 18: zone reading (b) passes under both speed readings (largest P 0.0066); zone reading (a) fails (P 0.08-0.79). The notebook picks (b) from the Supp. Fig. 1 panel titles, which the verifier could not verify. If the titles really fix the zone, the claims file left open a detail the paper gives, and supp1 would be reproduced (B2).

Cell 28: the criterion is met under O1 a. Under O1 b, no PPC layer has P < 0.05 (P = 0.07-0.52). The claims file's header requires blocked methods_underspecified when readings disagree, and adopting O1 a as an assumption conflicts with it; O1 a also fails to reproduce the class counts it is supposed to justify (B1).
Cell 30: met under O1 a (PM L2 vs L5, P = 0.0083). Under O1 b, PM L2 vs L5 has z = -0.88, P = 0.38. Readings disagree, so blocked by the claims file's rule (B1).

Blocked (other: not run, compute time). The data are present; too_large refers to the notebook's 14 h estimate, not to the data. The full 35 GB dataset was streamed in 40 min, so the data are not too large and the claim is testable (B8).

Cell 38: met only under O1 a with trace a. Every other combination has PM L5 intermittent 1 positive with P < 0.01. Adopting trace a and O1 a as assumptions conflicts with the claims file's rule (B1).
Cell 40: PPC 6/6 everywhere. PM is 4/6 under O1 a but 3/6 under O1 b (4 needed). It may shift with per-session k-means (B5).
Cell 42: met only under O1 b with trace b. Elsewhere, layer 3 at 25.1-8.4 cm is not significant.
Cell 44: group reading (a) fails under every O1/O3 reading; PM's median is nearer zero in 2 comparisons with P < 0.05. The criterion needs both group readings.

Cell 48: against the flat prior, 18/18 in all 8 configurations. Against permuted chance, 17/18 in 6 of 8 (PPC L3 intermittent 1 has z = +13.6). Reading (b) is not a real chance level: in F.decode(permute=True) the traces are time-warped by trial fraction, so every trial still runs 67 to 0 cm and the tuning survives; on a synthetic test the permuted chance decoder gave an RMSE of 1.07 cm, the same as the real decoder (B3, a claims-file issue).

Cell 52: met in 14 of 16 configurations. It fails under O1 b, shift 0.1, 0.42-cm bins, where PM is significantly lower in 1 bin. The NaN medians of layers 3 and 5 come from sessions without goal-distance neurons (B4).
Cell 54: met with 4.2-cm bins. With 0.42-cm bins, PM is closer with P < 0.01 in 3-8 bins under every configuration. Adopting 4.2 cm bins as an assumption conflicts with the claims file's rule (B1).
Cell 56: 100% of bins in 14 of 16 configurations and 99.8% in 2. Every reading gives at least partially.

Cell 62: PPC L3/L5 pass in 13-14 of the 16 tests required. In intermittent 1 at 8.4-0 cm the median slope is exactly 0: about 28% of trials have a constant MAP, which may be an argmax artifact of the 0.84-cm grid and was never checked (B10).
Blocked (other: not run, compute time). The data are present; the notebook's estimate is 1.4 h per reading, and the claim is testable (B8).

entries.name: funamizu-2016
entries.title: Dynamic Bayesian inference in mouse PPC and PM (Funamizu, Kuhn and Doya 2016)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Funamizu, Kuhn and Doya (2016) on dandiset 001605, which holds the two-photon imaging and behaviour of 94 sessions in 8 mice during auditory virtual navigation. It checks the session and neuron counts, licking behaviour, the classification of task-relevant neurons, the ramping of after-reaching neurons with and without sound, and the probabilistic decoding of goal distance. The muscimol experiment and the sound-mapping trials are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Funamizu et al. (2016) from dandiset 001605
